deep.reconstruction:
Setting. We are in a closed symmetric monoidal category (later a topos with ⊠ induced by ×). We have a pair of 'weak factorization' data: C (cofibrations) and TF (trivial fibrations), TC (trivial cofibrations) and F (fibrations). In each pair one class is defined by lifting against the other (C = LLP(TF), TF = RLP(C), and likewise for TC, F). For arrows i: A→B and i': A'→B', i'⊠i is the pushout-product A'×B ⊔_{A'×A} B'×A → B'×B. For i: A→B and f: X→Y, α(i,f) is the pullback-hom Hom(B,X) → Hom(A,X) ×_{Hom(A,Y)} Hom(B,Y). The only formal input is the adjunction α(i', α(i,f)) ≃ α(i'⊠i, f) together with symmetry of ⊠. From it follows the lifting duality: i'⊠i ⧄ f ⟺ i' ⧄ α(i,f) ⟺ i ⧄ α(i',f).

The page continues from the previous sheet. Grothendieck notes that to get closure of TC under ⊠ it is enough to know that i'⊠i ∈ TC when one factor is in TC and the other in C. He then records a dictionary.
- C⊠T ⊂ C (i×T for an object T, i.e. ⊠ with ∅→T) ⟺ TF stable under Hom(T,−).
- TC⊠T ⊂ TC ⟺ F stable under Hom(T,−).
- C⊠C ⊂ C ⟺ (i∈C, f∈TF ⇒ α(i,f)∈TF).
- TC⊠TC ⊂ TC (left side heavily crossed out) ⟺ (i∈TC, f∈F ⇒ α(i,f)∈F).
- TC⊠C ⊂ TC ⟺ (i∈C, f∈F ⇒ α(i,f)∈F). By the duality this is also ⟺ (i∈TC, f∈F ⇒ α(i,f)∈TF), as stated in the top lines.
This is the 'pushout-product / pullback-hom' calculus underlying Quillen's SM7 and the later monoidal-model-category axiom.

Example. Take a topos with ⊠ from the cartesian product, the usual internal Hom, and C = monomorphisms. Let I be a 'W-cylinder object' (an interval) with a section e: 1→I, possibly a whole given family of such intervals with sections. The generators (TC)_0 are the maps h(i0, A0, B0): A0×I ∪ B0×{e} ⊂ B0×I for arbitrary monos i0: A0→B0. That is, h(i0) = i0 ⊠ (e: 1→I), the 'Box e' annotation. TC is the class generated by (TC)_0.

Checks.
- C stable by ×T is trivial, so TF is stable by Hom(T,−).
- (TC)_0 is stable by ×T, since h(i0)×T = h(i0×id_T). Hence F is stable by Hom(T,−), and hence the saturated TC is stable by ×T.
- C⊠C ⊂ C: in a topos the pushout-product of monos is a mono.
- Still to check: TC⊠C ⊂ TC. For i = h(i0) and a mono i': A'→B', he sets up the square A'×A → B'×A, A'×B → B'×B, with B'×B = B'×B0×I.

The page stops there. The intended completion is the associativity argument h(i0)⊠i' = (i0⊠e)⊠i' ≅ (i0⊠i')⊠e = h(i0⊠i'). This lies in (TC)_0 because i0⊠i' is mono.

Purpose. The aim is a general recipe for (monoidal / Hom-compatible) homotopical structures on a topos, with cofibrations = monos and anodyne maps generated by an interval. Dating: the printout on the adjacent sheets (job 82160) gives June 1982, i.e. before Pursuing Stacks.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. The fourth equivalence is legible only after the crossing-out: the correct reading is TC⊠TC⊂TC ⟺ (i∈TC, f∈F ⇒ α(i,f)∈F). If the left side were read as C⊠TC, the right side would have to be ∈TF (equivalently i∈C, f∈F ⇒ α(i,f)∈F).

The equivalences tacitly require that C, TC, F, TF be saturated classes defined by lifting against each other (e.g. TC = LLP(F)). Also, in the example, TC must be taken as the saturation of (TC)_0; this is implicit.

The check TC⊠C ⊂ TC is left unfinished. The missing step, h(i0)⊠i' ≅ h(i0⊠i') by associativity and symmetry of the pushout-product, is easy. Passing from generators to the saturated class also needs the fact that ⊠ with a fixed mono preserves saturation; this follows from the α-adjunction just as for ×T.

Nothing on the page shows that the classes generated this way give a model structure (TC = C∩W for some W). With a single endpoint section e, this is a weaker statement than Cisinski's later theory, which also uses ∂I→I.

ideas.what: Lifting duality between pushout-product ⊠ and pullback-hom α: i'⊠i ⧄ f ⟺ i' ⧄ α(i,f), deduced formally from α(i',α(i,f)) ≃ α(i'⊠i,f)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (SM7, 1967) for the simplicial case; Hovey (1998–99), Schwede–Shipley (2000), Joyal–Tierney (2006–07) for the general formalism
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in Pursuing Stacks (1983); not certain

ideas.what: Dictionary of equivalences: stability of C, TC under ⊠ with objects and with each other ⟺ stability of TF, F under Hom(T,−) and under α
ideas.modern_name: Monoidal / enriched model category axioms (pushout-product axiom, SM7) in lifting form

ideas.what: On a topos, cofibrations = monos and anodyne maps generated by h(i0) = (A0×I ∪ B0×{e} ⊂ B0×I) for an interval I with section e (possibly a family of intervals), written as i0 ⊠ e
ideas.modern_name: Anodyne extensions associated with an elementary homotopical datum / exact cylinder (Cisinski's Λ_I(S)); Joyal's horn-type generating trivial cofibrations
ideas.usually_credited_to: D.-C. Cisinski (thesis 2002, Astérisque 308, 2006); earlier Gabriel–Zisman for simplicial anodyne extensions
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983) discusses homotopy intervals and model structures on presheaf toposes with monos as cofibrations; not sure this exact generator recipe appears there

ideas.what: Closure of generated anodyne class under pushout-product with monos via h(i0)⊠i' = h(i0⊠i')
ideas.modern_name: Stability of anodyne extensions under ⊠ with monomorphisms (Cisinski, Joyal)

missed.claim: Dated evidence (June 1982, from the IBM job-log printout on the adjacent sheets) that Grothendieck was already working on homotopical structures on an arbitrary topos before Pursuing Stacks. He took cofibrations = monos and generated trivial cofibrations from an interval with a section as h(i0) = i0⊠e, using the pushout-product/pullback-hom calculus. This anticipates the core of Cisinski's later theory of anodyne extensions on toposes.
missed.quote: C = mono, (TC)_0 = monomorphisms of the type (Box e) (A_0 × I) ⊂ B_0 × I, where A_0 → B_0 any mono, I any W-cylinder object endowed with section e
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It refines the historical record of the origin of Cisinski-type model structures on toposes and of Grothendieck's homotopy program (pre-1983). It shows he worked in the 'box product' lifting language independently of, and before, its codification by Hovey and Joyal–Tierney.

missed.claim: The verification TC⊠C ⊂ TC is started (pushout-product square for h(i0) and i') but not completed on this page. The next page is a computer printout, so the argument may continue elsewhere or not at all. The question of whether these classes form a model structure (identifying W) is not addressed here.
missed.quote: To check TC ⊠ C ⊂ TC, C ⊠ TC ⊂ TC. Consider i defined by i_0 : A_0 → B_0, I, e (i.e. i = h(i_0, A_0, B_0)) and i' : A' → B'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical. The missing step is now standard (Cisinski 2006).

deep.surprise_reason: The formalism itself is now standard. The point of interest is the early date (mid-1982, pre-Pursuing Stacks) at which Grothendieck had the pushout-product lifting calculus and the interval-generated anodyne class on a topos with monos as cofibrations. This anticipates Cisinski's theory, though Grothendieck's influence there via Pursuing Stacks is already acknowledged.
transcription_corrections: First line should read: 'provided we check that if i, i' ∈ TC (resp. i, i' ∈ C ?), then i'⊠i is in TC (resp. in C)'.
Second line: 'But this is so even if we assume only one of the two arrows i, i' in TC, the other being in C'.

The bottom diagram is the pushout-product square. Top row: A'×A → B'×A. Bottom row: A'×B ↪ B'×B = B'×B_0×I, with vertical inclusions. The 'A^*×A^{**}' and 'B'×B^*' readings are garbled forms of A'×A and B'×A.
The fourth equivalence's left side, under the crossings-out, appears to be TC⊠TC ⊂ TC, with right side (i∈TC, f∈F ⇒ α(i,f) ∈ F); the first line's left side is C⊠T ⊂ C.
The '(TC)_0 stable by ?×T' line continues '(replace i_0 by i_0 × id_T) hence F stable by Hom(T,?), hence TC stable by ?×T'.
The margin note reads approximately 'given bunch of I's with given sections'. It indicates a family of intervals rather than a single one.
The annotation over the usual Hom is uncertain; '(non-Schur)' is doubtful.
